A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FGSV research and provide readable text, equations, figures, and appendices. V1 Appendices A and B match v2 Appendices B and C; v2 adds a proof appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original SOU simulations, Stable Diffusion copyright-attribution experiments, Diabetes regression experiments, and supplementary runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical studies and additionally reports final absolute-relative-error results for the SOU benchmark in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The sampling rule following Eq. (11) changes the base subset size from |S|=s-1 to |S|=s, changing the sizes of evaluated sets as written. FGSV's definition and the algorithms' overall structure remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this local change was implemented.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture motivational example, SOU games, FlickrLogo-27 copyright-attribution task, and Diabetes regression task. The tested splitting and demographic-grouping scenarios are unchanged; the expanded copier-attack discussion introduces no evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 retains Permutation, Group Testing, Complementary Contribution, One-for-All, KernelSHAP, Unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP. The GSV and SRS application comparisons also remain unchanged. Revised Group Testing citations do not correspond to a changed estimator in the experimental appendix.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 adds final absolute relative error (ARE) alongside AUCC and runtime. The 20,000-evaluation budget, four-group allocation, and n=64,128,256 settings remain unchanged, as do the application experiments' splits, models, and training settings.

E4.justification: The shell-company splitting examples, Diabetes regrouping analysis, and Figure 5 subset-size runtime diagnostic are retained. No new ablation, sensitivity test, robustness experiment, or case study is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 30 SOU replications, 30 Diabetes Monte Carlo replications, and Figure 5's 50 sampled subsets per size. Standard-deviation reporting and seed information are unchanged. The added ARE boxplots extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 2 adds final ARE distributions, reporting the lowest average ARE for FGSV, and revises existing AUCC distributions and runtime bars. At n=256, the largest runtime bar changes from KernelSHAP to Group Testing. Results displayed in Figures 1, 3, 4, and 5 are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds Appendix A with proofs of Theorems 1–3, Propositions 1–3, and Lemma 1, including new interpolation definitions and supporting lemmas. Theorem 3 adds an explicit error bound but omits previously stated Assumptions 1–2, which its proof still uses. Proposition 2 removes the s^-2 rate cap, although Appendix A.6 derives the capped rate.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about faithful valuation, uniqueness, and efficient approximation remain unchanged. Section 5 adds a conditional capability claim: incorporating a Pearl do-operation utility can also defend against copier attacks, extending v1's preprocessing suggestion and open-problem statement.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes self-replication from pure infringement, qualifies the availability of do-operation utilities, and discusses limitations of submodular replication defenses. It also adds interpretations of the SGD smoothness assumptions and states an efficiency advantage when evaluating o(n) groups.

D1.justification: Section 3.4 newly suggests B=cp for linear regression with p predictors and describes label shuffling to construct the non-informative distribution. These clarify the existing augmentation scheme. Experimental hyperparameters, hardware, implementation descriptions, and code-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Falconer et al. and Han et al. on replication robustness, positioning shell-company attacks relative to copier attacks. McLeod and Zorich references support the new proofs, and Group Testing references are revised. This is a focused expansion of positioning and citations.

P1.justification: V2 locally expands the introduction, methodological explanations, and conclusion, and makes terminology and affiliation edits. It inserts a proof appendix with a contents list and renumbers the existing appendices. The main section sequence and most original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 expands from two rows to three by adding ARE panels, relocates its legend, and revises its caption and axes. Figures 3 and 4 move with the text reflow. The other figure graphics and both algorithm displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new proof appendix substantially improves inspectability of previously unproved claims, while ARE reporting and attack qualifications add useful detail. However, Eq. (11)'s revised sampling conflicts with its unchanged size-s target, Proposition 2 claims a faster rate than Appendix A.6 derives, and Theorem 3 omits assumptions required by its proof. These gains and regressions concern the central algorithm and guarantees, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
